thread:
anya: Quick heads-up: during int4 onboarding for orpheus-32k I saw an output divergence only when KV streaming + compaction is enabled. FP16 baseline OK.

samir: How far into the context? and which quant packer?

anya: ~18k tokens (around 17910-17995 region). quantizer = per-shard int4 packer (v1). The compile chose rotary kernel 'rot_v1' due to short-seq fallback.

jess: Does the same behavior happen with streaming disabled?

anya: No. With streaming off + full prefill the sequence matches fp16. With streaming on we see subtle prob shifts then eventual different continuations.

samir: That smells like an index mapping problem when compaction / shrink runs in the broker. Any recent broker changes?

anya: Yes, PR#4123 touched ringbuffer shrink heuristics and compaction. I can repro quickly with a synthetic pad.

anya: Running quick repro:
```
python experiments/quick_kv_repro.py --model orpheus-32k-int4 --pad-to 17920 --stream true --random-seed 42
```
It shows duplicate kv index emitted at compaction time. Log snippet:
```
[compactor] shrink -> removed 128 slots, new_tail=17993
[runtime] kv_emit shard=3 idx=17992 fid=0x8c3a
[runtime] kv_emit shard=3 idx=17992 fid=0x8c3a  <-- duplicate detected
```

jess: Do we have kv fingerprints to compare between fp16 run and int4 streaming run?

anya: Pushed both fingerprints and logits to s3: s3://redwood-ml/eng-ml/repro/kvdup/17920_int4_stream_fp.json and ..._fp16.json

samir: If duplicate index occurs, the KV lookup may return stale vector or wrong position leading to token shift. Hypothesis: compaction sets new_tail but we don't update in-flight mapping for some shards.

jess: Could also be rot kernel choosing older rot_v1 which misinterprets absolute positions after wrap. Try forcing rot_v2 + rope_clamp=true and see if it still repros.

anya: I'll run three quick variants: (A) int4 + streaming + rot_v1 (baseline repro), (B) int4 + streaming + rot_v2 + clamp, (C) int4 + no-streaming. I also plan to run broker binary from before PR#4123 to see if compaction is the root cause.

devops-bot: Canary deploy queued for branch revert/pr4123-rollback on pool=dedicated-canary by @samir. ETA 12m.

samir: Also instrument runtime to increment telemetry counter KV_COMPACTION_DUP for every duplicate idx detected so we can see prod rates.

anya: Added a lightweight counter and a log flag; pushed to my branch. Synthetic test triggers counter 1->2 times per run.

jess: If old broker binary doesn't show duplicates, then we either revert or add a compaction safety-check that verifies no in-flight mappings point to removed slots. Safer guard first.

samir: Agree, guard + metric + quick canary revert. If guard causes perf regress, fallback to revert. We should also add a unit test in broker that creates holes and exercises shrink.

anya: Noted. I'll attach repro archive once full run finishes (~20m). For now I uploaded quick-trace tar to s3://redwood-ml/eng-ml/repro/kvdup/quicktrace-17920.tar.gz

jess: Great. After we validate guard, let's run the full goldset eval to confirm int4 matches fp16 with streaming enabled. Also record per-token KL divergence as part of eval.

anya: Will do. Quick sample from the log where divergence first appears:
```
[17908] tok="to" p=0.041 -> p_fp16=0.042
[17909] tok="ensure" p=0.012 -> p_fp16=0.011
[17910] tok="we" p=0.035 -> p_fp16=0.036
[17911] tok="haven't" p=0.002 -> p_fp16=0.009
[17912] tok="." p=0.008 -> p_fp16=0.021  <-- gap widens
```

samir: Perfect. That log plus kv fingerprints should be enough to triage. Thanks Anya. Ping once you have kernel+guard comparison and I'll coordinate the canary. :rocket:

anya: Will do. :thumbsup:
